questions.q:
With reference to the National Commission for Women's push for women-led development and property rights, consider the following statements:
1. Articles 38, 39 and 46 reflect the idea of distributive justice.
2. Section 396 of the BNSS deals with victim compensation schemes.
3. In Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020), a daughter's coparcenary right was held to depend on her father being alive on the date of the 2005 amendment.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Vineeta Sharma held that coparcenary rights arise by birth, whether or not the father was alive on the amendment date. Compensatory justice, by contrast, remedies past discrimination (Articles 17 and 23, reservations, victim compensation). The NCW urged a shift from welfare to women as leaders, with women's shares recorded in digitised land records.

questions.q:
With reference to the Protein Sovereignty Index, consider the following statements:
1. It is published by the Food and Agriculture Organization.
2. India ranked 17th and was placed in the 'Exposed' category.
3. India imports less than a quarter of its fertiliser supply by value.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The index is by Full Circle Biotechnology, assessing 43 countries; Canada (82.8) is the only 'Sovereign' country. India (62.1) imports 68.6% of its fertiliser by value and over 90% of rock phosphate, and urea depends on imported gas, so Hormuz disruptions threaten protein supply.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding India's protein security:
1. India's renewable freshwater availability, about 1,014 cubic metres per person, is below the water-stress threshold of 1,700.
2. India imported a record 7.34 million tonnes of pulses in 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Pulse imports were about a fifth of supply, as pulse area fell from 30.6 to 26.9 million hectares. SOFI 2026 says 520.1 million Indians (35.5%) could not afford a healthy diet in 2025, and the poorest decile eats only 38% of the recommended eggs, fish and meat.

questions.q:
With reference to the NSS 80th Round (2025) on health, consider the following statements:
1. The share of people reporting ailments rose in both rural and urban areas compared with 2017-18.
2. Health-insurance coverage in rural areas rose to about 47%.
3. In rural areas, average hospitalisation cost in private facilities was about seven times that in government facilities.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct: ailments rose to 12.2% (rural) and 14.9% (urban), rural insurance to 47.4%, and rural costs were Rs 47,710 private against Rs 6,905 public. Yet out-of-pocket spending stays high, a 'medical poverty trap', so the magazine urges stronger public care from Ayushman Arogya Mandirs upward rather than relying on insurance alone.

questions.q:
With reference to price control of medicines in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013 is issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
2. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority was set up in 1997.
3. Scheduled formulations are based on the National List of Essential Medicines, which has 384 medicines.
4. The ceiling price formula includes a 16% retailer margin.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The ceiling price is the average price to retailer of brands with at least 1% market share plus a 16% margin, revised every 1 April by WPI. The Supreme Court called the PTR-MRP gap 'broad daylight dacoity' and asked why the 16% margin should not apply to all essential medicines, citing a cancer drug marked up tenfold.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Non-scheduled drugs can be launched at very high MRPs that escape price control.
Statement-II: The 10% cap on annual price increases of non-scheduled drugs applies only to increases after launch, not to the launch price itself.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. This 'launch-price loophole' was raised before the Supreme Court along with hospital markups, such as an antibiotic sold at Rs 5,635 in a corporate hospital against Rs 350 outside. Suggested fixes include curbing launch MRPs for critical non-NLEM drugs and more Jan Aushadhi generics.

questions.q:
With reference to the Allahabad High Court's ruling on hookah service in Uttar Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. It held that restaurants cannot serve hookah even in Designated Smoking Areas.
2. Under COTPA, Designated Smoking Areas are permitted in restaurants with seating capacity of 50 or more.
3. The Supreme Court in Narinder S. Chadha (2014) had held that hookah could not be served in Designated Smoking Areas.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. COTPA allows Designated Smoking Areas in hotels with 30+ rooms, restaurants seating 30+ and airports. Chadha (2014) read the old Rule 4(3), barring 'other' services, as allowing hookah but not food; the 2017 amendment dropped 'other', so the HC held no service at all is allowed, herbal hookah included. A one-hour session is about 200 puffs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding WHO's first guidelines on child and adolescent obesity:
1. They are WHO's first guidelines on how health systems should manage obesity in children and adolescents.
2. They recommend medicines, under supervision, for obese children aged 0-9 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. For ages 0-9 the guidelines rule out drugs, bariatric surgery and devices; for 10-19, medicines may be used if supervised lifestyle measures fail, and surgery only in severe cases. India has about 14 million obese children per the World Obesity Atlas 2026, second only to China.

questions.q:
Which of the following have been declared fully literate under ULLAS - New India Literacy Programme?
1. Mizoram
2. Tripura
3. Bihar
4. Lakshadweep
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Uttarakhand, and the UTs of Ladakh, Chandigarh, A&N Islands, J&K and now Lakshadweep, have been declared fully literate, meaning at least 95% literacy. ULLAS is a centrally sponsored scheme for 2022-27, aligned with NEP 2020, for non-literates aged 15 and above.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding care for the elderly:
1. Article 41 is a Fundamental Right guaranteeing public assistance in old age.
2. The Union Budget 2026-27 announced training for 1.5 lakh caregivers aligned to the NSQF.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Article 41 is a Directive Principle, not an enforceable right. India's 60+ population is projected to grow from about 149 million (2022) to 347 million by 2050. Keralam passed a Senior Citizens Bill, 2026 to regulate care facilities, and NITI's 'Reimagining Care' report proposes a National Caregiver Council.

questions.q:
With reference to the World Bank's Poverty and Equity Brief on India (October 2026), consider the following statements:
1. Extreme poverty at $3 a day fell to below 1% in 2023-24.
2. The brief is published once a year as part of the World Development Report.
3. At the $4.20 line, poverty is higher in urban than in rural areas.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Extreme poverty at $3 a day fell from 27.1% (2011-12) to 2.6% (2023-24). The brief is published twice a year for the Spring and Annual Meetings. At $4.20 a day, rural poverty is 19.3% against urban 8.6%, and about 57% of the poor live in the belt from UP to West Bengal; youth unemployment rose from 14.6% to 15.9%.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the NMC's guidelines on advertising by doctors and hospitals:
1. Repeated violations can lead to permanent removal of the doctor's name from the register.
2. They bar patient and celebrity testimonials, including AI-generated testimonials, images or voices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Penalties are graded: a warning and ethics training, censure and fine, suspension for 3-6 months (6-12 for serious cases), and removal from the register for 1-3 years for repeated violations. The guidelines also bar referral fees and unverifiable 'No. 1' claims; enforcement by State Medical Councils is uneven.

questions.q:
With reference to the regulation of AI-based medical devices in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Medical Devices Rules, 2017 classify devices into risk classes A, B, C and D.
2. State licensing authorities license the manufacture of Class C and D devices.
3. CDSCO's July 2026 guidance on medical device software has the force of a statute.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. States license Class A and B manufacture, while the Central Licensing Authority licenses Class C and D and all imports. The guidance, which distinguishes software in a device (SiMD) from stand-alone software (SaMD) and demands Indian validation and bias data, is not binding law, and the parent Drugs and Cosmetics Act dates from 1940.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the reuse of single-use medical devices:
1. The Directorate General of Health Services directed all public and private facilities to stop reusing single-use devices.
2. The Medical Devices Rules, 2017 require single-use devices to be labelled as such.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Hospitals were sterilising and reusing catheters, guidewires and dialysis items, sometimes billing full price, risking hepatitis B and C, HIV and device failure. Gaps remain: no new penalties or inspection schedule, few Medical Device Officers, and several States have not adopted the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010.

questions.q: PRASHAST, through which the Department of School Education screened an inclusive-education module in 2026, is
o: a scholarship portal for students with disabilities
a school-based digital tool for screening probable disabilities among children
a teacher-recruitment platform for special educators
questions.e: PRASHAST (Pre-Assessment Holistic Screening Tool) lets teachers screen children for probable disabilities under the RPwD Act, 2016, after which special educators validate and refer them. The 30-minute module on Children with Special Needs, in 12 languages, targets heads, teachers and non-teaching staff in a whole-school approach under NEP 2020.
